ranking.name: Provider-minted clock bracket on client log stamps (server request/response ids per stream; Gemini HTTP Date and server-timing as the aiv_cu leg)
merged_from: power#1 Server-minted id bracket and binding test
robustness#1 Provider-clock ceiling on each tool round
coverage#1 Server-minted request-id bracket as a stretch guard for latency checks
coverage#4 Provider-clock action windows for logs without per-call stamps (AI Village computer use)
ranking.observation: Honest rate: one constant client-server skew per stream places every decoded request-id time between the stream's last input event and its first output block in all but 10 of 3,674 swechat Claude Code streams, rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466] (session-clustered, tolerance 2 s; 18 at 0 s, 7 at 5 s); slack U-L p5 1,102 / p50 2,268 / p95 3,807 ms; cc_local 1 of 847 streams (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O5 skeptic_numbers; the committed lens output has 10/3,676, same rate, 1,610 sessions: analysis/out/phase_c/ids_and_clocks_in_ids.json bracket.swechat.anthropic_req.claude_code). Of the 10 inconsistent swechat sessions, 2 hold re-stamped resume/fork copies, so 8 are unexplained (ids_and_clocks_in_ids.json bracket_x_copies.swechat). Measured tamper displacement (placebo on 3,673 swechat streams, one response's first event moved): 5 s earlier flags 1,441 streams, 30 s earlier flags 3,581, and 5/30/300 s later flag 10, which equals the baseline (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json ids/O5 skeptic_numbers; also analysis/out/phase_c/_verification_ir.json). No CI is stored for these placebo counts, and they were produced by an uncommitted scratchpad script (rd/o5c.py), so FINDINGS cannot cite them under rule 1 until they are re-run from a committed script. The roll-every-response result (3,667/3,673) misbinds all responses at once and does not measure splicing of a single response (grounding skeptic, analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[0].ground.checks[0]). Clock agreement counting every copy: 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992] in 1,638 sessions; split-A holdout 11,047 ids, 0 violations (ids/O2 skeptic). Layout (base58 UUIDv7 behind req_01): 154,815/154,815 swechat and 31,085/31,085 cc_local ids v7|var2 against 2,418.98 expected by chance; UNVERIFIED against documentation (ids/O1). aiv_cu leg: Gemini server-timing dur fits inside the DB row gap with 0/12,292 violations (Wilson hi 3.12e-4, 347 of 2,000 B sessions, min slack 563.8 ms) (two_clocks/O7 skeptic). aiv_cu id brackets: 0 inconsistent Anthropic (105/80/27/32 streams) and Gemini (255/92) streams, 3/463 OpenAI; the skeptic calls the aiv_cu id test weak by construction (row insert lags the id by a median 5.7-12 s; OpenAI and Gemini ids have 1 s resolution) (ids/O3, O5).
ranking.test_measurement: (1) Commit the placebo code (o5/o5b/o5c) as a probe script and re-run it so the tamper numbers have committed provenance. (2) Single-response tamper suite on swechat CC streams and cc_local (847 streams), session-clustered CIs, at the measured honest rate: delay one tool_result by D in {1, 2, 5, 30, 300} s with every id untouched (the mirror of the measured output back-dating; never run); insert one fabricated call+result round; splice one response with its request id from another session or from later in the same session; back-date one response on a 1-30 s grid to find the displacement at power 0.5 and 0.9, for comparison with U-L p50 2,268 ms. Report power per tamper type, not pooled. (3) Ceiling leg (robustness#1, never run): S = t_req(k+1) - t_req(k) against every client duration for that round (call->result gap, bash_progress elapsed, durationMs, totalDurationMs); report honest slack (S-D)/S and violations per timer type. (4) aiv_cu Gemini header leg (coverage#4): w = created_at - HTTP Date per row, by action; positive controls (pause, explicit sleep) must satisfy w >= requested duration - 1 s; then separability of long-work vs trivial shell outputs (unmeasured). Split hygiene: this lens already read B and the split-A holdout, so fix tolerances now and test on cc_local sessions recorded after the Phase C commit.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 10/3,674 honest swechat streams (2 explained by re-stamped resume/fork copies, 8 unexplained) and 1/847 cc_local; the count moves with tolerance (18 at 0 s, 7 at 5 s) (ids/O5; bracket_x_copies). Within-session client clock drift above 2 s in 15 swechat sessions and in 2 of 18 cc_local sessions; a constant skew is absorbed but a step is not (ids/O6 skeptic). 12 offsets over 10 min remain after dedupe, unexplained (ids/O2 skeptic). Gap-0 call->result pairs: bulk re-stamping explains 169/498; 329 v2.1 gap-0 pairs are unexplained and would hit any zero-width window rule (two_clocks/O12 skeptic). Second-resolution OpenAI/Gemini ids and the 1 s HTTP Date (415 flash and 1,714 pro rows lie within 1 s of the insert; distributions/D19 skeptic). Ceiling leg: background/async launches (cc_local parent result before last nested event 63/63; two_clocks/O15). Unmeasured: provider server-to-server skew between consecutive ids, retries, concurrent subagent streams.
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - prior art not checked; do not claim new. Time-in-identifier forensics (UUIDv1, ULID, Snowflake) is a known general technique, and the grounding skeptic recalls (itself unverified) that Gladyshev & Patel's event-time-bounding work bounds an event between causally ordered timestamped events with a clock-offset allowance, which is the bracket's logic. If anything is new it would be using LLM-provider request ids (and Gemini Date/server-timing headers) as the bound on agent tool-log stamps; that is a guess. HTTP Date as a forensic artefact is known.
ranking.why_this_rank: (a) The only merged mechanism with a measured tamper displacement against a measured honest rate (honest 10/3,674 streams; 5 s and 30 s back-dating flag 1,441 and 3,581 of 3,673). (b) The witness is minted by the provider at request receipt and the model never writes stamps or ids, but the ids are unsigned and re-mintable by anyone who knows the inferred layout. It constrains only post-hoc log edits that move a response earlier or (untested) a result later. In-band fabrication is stamped consistently by the harness and is invisible, and a lying tool backend behind an honest harness gets nothing beyond Probe 1 (grounding skeptics, analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[0..2].ground.checks[0]). It is one-sided: later output shifts flag only the baseline 10. (c) Two of five scaffold families: swechat CC (155,267 (session, request) pairs, 1,638 sessions) and cc_local (31,085 ids). aiv_cc stores 0 request ids (ids/O13); Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI have only client-minted ids; Who&When has no clock; the share of tool calls covered is unmeasured. (d) Cheapest next step, since the placebo code exists. Penalties applied: the power lens's 'only measured tamper curve' claim is false (TC2 has one); 3,667/3,673 overreads; ids/O7 is not independent evidence; aiv_cu support is weak by construction; the stretch-guard power (coverage#1) and the ceiling (robustness#1) are entirely unmeasured. It still ranks first on criterion (a).

ranking.name: Provider image-token quanta as a screenshot-count ledger (Gemini prompt IMAGE units; aiv_cc stripped-image residual as a one-agent leg)
merged_from: power#4 Quantized server-usage ledger of result modality (per-image and cache-block units)
robustness#5 Provider quantization lattices in usage fields as a trap for synthesized rounds
coverage#5 Image-token quanta as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents
ranking.observation: aiv_cu Gemini, split B: the per-window change in prompt IMAGE tokens is 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11,668/11,668 pairs (258 for gemini-2.5-pro, n 4,925; 1064 for 3-pro 682, 3.1-pro 3,166, 3.5-flash 2,895), never negative; positive in 5,059/5,092 GUI windows and 0 in shell 0/4,134, get_pixel_coords 0/2,033 and pause 0/202 windows (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json token_conservation/TC9 skeptic_numbers). Prompt IMAGE counts sit on {258, 1064, 2160} in 10,569/10,569 pro rows and on 1064 in 3,219/3,219 flash rows; no session mixes lattices (0/309) (distributions/D3 skeptic). aiv_cc (single-agent case study): residual per stripped image median 890.1 [887.9, 890.9], p25 879.1, p75 892.7, n 4,543 single-image pairs in 64 runs; 227 of those pairs fall in the 316-562 bin, below the honest per-turn |residual| p99 of 690.2 (651-735 across splits), so single-image power there is below 1 and unmeasured (aiv_accounting/O11 and O10 skeptic; analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[0].ground.checks[3]). Dropped from the merge per the grounding skeptic (analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[1].ground.checks[4]): the usage_in mode (D7, 0.835 for opus-4-6, a modal value not a lattice) and the Codex reasoning lattice (D1, 140/6,910 on-lattice). The Codex 128-multiple rule (16,106/16,106, swechat_tables/T11) is kept only as a note: found post hoc, and an informed forger satisfies it trivially.
ranking.test_measurement: On aiv_cu Gemini (11,945 conservation pairs): predict IMAGE units per window from the logged action types and require dIMAGE = units x per-model constant. Tamper honest windows by deleting one GUI result, relabelling a GUI action as shell, inserting a fabricated screenshot-returning call and result, and splicing in a window from another session. Report detection per direction at the measured honest rates (33/5,092 GUI windows with no increment; 0 in non-GUI windows), with session-clustered CIs and a session-level false-positive rate, which no file states yet. Test the regime above 40 images: no B session reached it, while 442 population Gemini sessions exceed 40 GUI turns. aiv_cc: count [IMAGE_REMOVED] markers per window and measure single-image power at FPR 1%, run-clustered, labelled one agent. Optional: refit aiv_cu Anthropic conservation with an image term (TC1 left it out; GUI windows residual median +206.5 vs shell -602.8) to see whether a quantum exists there.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5,092 GUI windows with no increment, unexplained and not cap effects (images before: median 4, max 31) (TC9 skeptic). The unit changes with model generation (258, 1064, and 2160 in 70 rows from 3 sessions; D3). gemini-3.8-flash (277 pairs) never shows an image. Cached IMAGE counts are off-lattice (11/3,022 and 40/9,318), so only prompt-side counts are checkable (D3). aiv_cc has 30 unlogged non-compaction context resets, 27 of them image pairs (aiv_accounting/O12). User-pasted images vary in size (swechat CC single-image residual 535.0, p5-p95 121-1,618; TC17), so a per-image constant holds only for fixed-size screenshots. Per-window misses compound at session level; no session-level rate exists.
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - prior art not checked; do not claim new. Both grounding skeptics find no overlap with the listed items, but plausibility checks on billed token counts and on value distributions (Benford-style) are old and generic. Using a provider's per-modality token breakdown as an exact count of image-returning results in an agent log may be undescribed; that is a guess.
ranking.why_this_rank: (a) The honest data are exact: 11,668/11,668 on-lattice increments and zero increments in every non-GUI window (0/4,134 shell, 0/2,033 get_pixel_coords, 0/202 pause), at one-image resolution, with no post-hoc exclusion list needed for the non-GUI direction. No tamper simulation has been run, so detection power is inferred from arithmetic, not measured. (b) Server-computed and, by reasoning rather than observation, never in the model's context. An informed log editor can recompute it but must shift IMAGE and promptTokenCount by exact units in every later response, because screenshots stay in context (up to 40 observed). A live forger who returns a real screenshot gets a real increment, and the ledger witnesses count, not content. (c) Narrowest coverage of the five: the exact ledger exists only in aiv_cu Gemini (Gemini rows with timing in 347 of 2,000 B sessions, two_clocks/O7) plus one aiv_cc agent. It covers GUI logs, where text checks fail (STOP narration string support 0.657 at gui_0 vs 0.286 at gui_gt_half; GUI results carry text in 0.0002 of rows; aiv_narration/N5 skeptic). (d) Cheap: the counts already exist. Ranked above ranks 3 and 4 because its honest exactness does not rest on an in-sample whitelist and its witness is server-computed rather than same-writer; below rank 1 because it has no measured tamper rate and covers one family.

ranking.name: Execution-window consistency: fresh clock evidence in a result (resolved git commit dates; printed durations) must fit that result's own call->result window and harness timers
merged_from: robustness#3 Nested timer chain (printed durations <= harness timers <= provider interval)
ranking.observation: Git leg (swechat, Entire-linked Claude Code sessions): a commit SHA printed in a Bash result resolves for 3,936 claims in 1,491 sessions, and commit_date lies in [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s] for 3,917 = 0.995 [0.992, 0.998]; median offset -0.103 s (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json commit_witness/O9 skeptic). Of the 19 out-of-window claims, 15 are cat/tail/head/grep re-reads of earlier output files, 1 is an amend with explicit GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, 3 are unexplained; this classification was made after seeing the 19 (commit_witness/O11 skeptic). 2,198/6,141 = 0.358 [0.321, 0.394] of honest commit claims do not resolve (commit_witness/O10 skeptic). Harness-timer legs: bash_progress floor rule 0/112,677 events (Wilson hi 3.41e-5, 687 sessions), result after last tick 5,676/5,676 (two_clocks/O9 skeptic); the Codex model-visible Wall time header never exceeds the call->output gap for exec_command, 0/4,408 at 2 ms (5 sessions; 1 supplies 1,604/2,420 own-end rows), while 0.1 s-display shell_command headers exceed it in 646/1,817 by <= 49 ms (two_clocks/O6 skeptic). The grounding skeptic says these timer legs are written from the same process clock as the stamps, so 'inside the window' is close to tautological; only commit_date and fresh readings printed by generator commands are execution-side evidence (analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[0].ground.checks[2]). Fraction-form printed epochs never postdate the external wiki save, 0/459 (Wilson upper 0.0083), but that is collusion-wiki only, one-sided, and the with-fraction split is post hoc (ext_witness/O10). The printed-duration content leg (test-runner 'in X s', shell 'real') was never extracted: its coverage and honest rate are unmeasured.
ranking.test_measurement: Pre-register on split A the re-reader command list from commit_witness/O11 and regexes for printed durations. (1) Measure the share of tool results carrying a fresh absolute reading or a printed duration, with a stop rule if the share is too small to matter. (2) Honest violation rate per command class with session-clustered CIs; tolerance 2 s for commit dates, the printed resolution for durations. (3) Tamper suite: replay a real clock-bearing output from earlier in the session or from another session; shift stamps on a delta grid. (4) Lying-backend simulation: keep printed text such as 'N passed in 45 s' but give the call an instant-return timing profile drawn from honest calls; and a padded backend that sleeps for the printed duration, which should pass and measures the forger's wall-clock cost. Report power vs delta at the honest rate.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: re-reads of saved output (15 of 19 out-of-window commit claims), explicit committer dates (1), 3 unexplained of 3,936 resolved claims; display rounding (Codex shell_command 646/1,817 by <= 49 ms); write_stdin poll stamps (14/1,600, min -36.1 ms); machine suspend (1 progress event over its timeout among 83,521; two_clocks/O10); 329 v2.1 gap-0 pairs outside any tie block, unexplained (two_clocks/O12 skeptic); auto-backgrounded commands whose result window is not the execution window (111 of 188 swechat 120 s shell results; outliers/O9 as applied in analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[0]); stored ids and dates echoed by tools (440 of 561 v7 uuid mentions in results are more than 10 min older; ids/O14). Non-resolving SHAs (0.358 of honest claims) make a missing SHA unusable on its own.
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - prior art not checked; do not claim new. Partly prior art per the grounding skeptics: the git leg is a claim-vs-record existence check that overlaps our own git shadow-state core plan, and the window logic is event-time bounding (Gladyshev & Patel line, listed). Bounding non-recomputable outputs by the log's own clock (unlike METR-style recomputation of echo/wc) might be less common; extracting printed durations is output-grammar parsing (jc).
ranking.why_this_rank: (b) is its strength: commit_date is hashed into the SHA and the commit lives in an external repo, so moving or inventing a resolving commit claim needs a real commit with a chosen committer date in that repo (the skeptic corrects 'needs a real commit made at that time', since committer dates can be set). Its printed-duration leg is the only proposal aimed at a lying tool backend behind an honest harness, which ranks 1 and 2 cannot see. (a) is weaker than ranks 1-2: no tamper rate measured; the 3-unexplained figure depends on a post-hoc command classification; the timer legs are near-tautological. (c) Git leg only in swechat Entire-linked CC sessions (3,936 resolved claims); progress ticks are absent in current Claude Code (0/332 cc_local main files; raw_census/A6-O10); the share of results carrying any fresh clock is unmeasured. (d) Moderate: needs command classification, regexes and git lookups. Rank 4 edges it on (a) by count exactness and n, but neither has a measured tamper rate and both rest on post-hoc exclusion lists the skeptics flagged, so I let (b), where they differ sharply, break the near-tie.

ranking.name: Dual-rendering recount: Claude Code's harness structured result copy (Read numLines, subagent totalToolUseCount, Edit/Grep counters) vs the model-visible result text
merged_from: power#2 Visible-text vs harness structured-copy recount at 1-unit resolution
coverage#3 Dual-rendering check: harness-only structured result fields vs the model-visible result text
ranking.observation: Read toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the line-numbered lines of the model-visible text in 87,827/88,229 = 0.9954, Wilson [0.9950, 0.9959], cluster [0.9947, 0.9960], 4,603 files (full swechat population); all 402 mismatches are named harness or dataset formats (282 persisted-output previews, 105 'file shorter than offset' warnings, 7 identical-to references, 7 redactions, 1 negative line numbers); cc_local main 570/578, all 8 empty-file warnings (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json raw_census/A6-O1 skeptic). Subagent totalToolUseCount equals distinct nested tool_use ids in 6,623/6,623, Wilson [0.9994, 1.0], 1,934 files; 2,150/8,773 = 0.245 [0.236, 0.254] of Agent/Task results have no nested traffic and cannot be checked (A6-O2 skeptic). Field fill: Read 88,229/90,763 = 0.972, Edit structuredPatch 70,553/73,460 = 0.960, Grep numLines 29,535/34,208 = 0.863; agreement of Edit/Grep counters with the text is not measured (A6-O4 skeptic). The skeptic's mechanical explanation: one harness writes both fields from the same read, so this is internal redundancy, not an independent witness.
ranking.test_measurement: Freeze the whitelist now and measure the honest unexplained rate on data it was not derived from (cc_local sessions recorded after the Phase C commit); the existing 0 is in-sample. Tamper a random sample of clean Read results: add or delete 1, 2 or 5 lines; splice a same-path Read result from another session; substitute content with the line count held; and rewrite a result into a whitelisted format (preview, offset warning, identical-to reference) to measure the whitelist as an evasion route. Do the same for A6-O2 by deleting or inserting one nested tool_use. Then measure agreement, not presence, for Grep numLines and for Edit structuredPatch oldLines/newLines against old_string/new_string line counts.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: the 402 swechat whitelisted formats and cc_local's 8 empty-file warnings would all fire without the whitelist, and the whitelist was built from those same mismatches, so the honest unexplained rate of 0 is in-sample (analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json lenses[0].ground.checks[1]). Blind spots: 2,150/8,773 Agent/Task results uncheckable; cc_local subagent files carry no Read numLines (0 of 12); Glob totalMatches absent in swechat (0/6,422); the subagent-count leg has no coverage on current Claude Code, because cc_local has 0 progress/agent_progress entries in 332 main and 840 subagent files (raw_census/A6-O10).
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - prior art not checked; do not claim new. The two grounding skeptics disagree: power#2's finds none of the listed items; coverage#3's finds substantial overlap (recounting numbered lines is output-grammar parsing, jc, plus recomputation, METR; the cross-call part is our own filesystem shadow-state core plan). Consistency between redundant fields is a generic data-integrity idea.
ranking.why_this_rank: (a) Tightest honest agreement at the largest n of any proposal (88,229 Read results; 6,623 subagent counts) at 1-line resolution, but the 0-unexplained figure is in-sample and no tamper rate is measured. (b) Weakest witness of the five: both renderings come from one writer, a schema-aware editor recomputes the counter trivially, count-preserving substitution is invisible, and under an execution-layer compromise both renderings derive from the same fake output. It catches only a naive post-hoc text editor or a harness/export fault. (c) Claude Code formats in practice (the Codex Wall-time pair rests on 5 sessions); the subagent leg is absent from current Claude Code. (d) Cheapest to build. Fourth because criterion (b) is where it fails, and the skeptics flag an in-sample overclaim and partial prior-art overlap.

ranking.name: Usage-ledger reconciliation frozen at commit time (Entire CLI tally at tolerance 0), with parameter-free usage identities such as the prompt-cache chain
merged_from: power#5 Frozen usage-ledger reconciliation at tolerance 0
robustness#4 Prompt-cache state as a server-computed stopwatch and unchanged-prefix certificate (folded in as the cache-chain sub-leg; its stopwatch claim is not supported)
ranking.observation: A 5-integer token/API tally written by the Entire CLI at commit time equals, at tolerance 0, a recount of the stored transcript (whole, prefix or window) in 4,794/4,836 = 0.9913 [0.9883, 0.9936] Claude-format sessions, repo-clustered [0.9874, 0.9942] over 183 repos; prefix sessions are snapshots taken while the session continued (created_at before the last transcript timestamp in 1,664/1,664) (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json swechat_tables/T1 skeptic). After correcting a dataset join artifact, 33/5,701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] remain unmatched across 4 scaffolds (T3 skeptic); by CLI version 0.4.x 11/3,691 = 0.0030 [0.0017, 0.0053], 0.5.x 15/1,048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235] (T4 skeptic). The skeptic says the tally is a deterministic recount of the transcript's own usage fields: its only independent content is the commit-time snapshot, and it says nothing about whether a tool result is real. Cache chain cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean swechat CC / cc_local / aiv_cc pairs (TC1 skeptic) and in 59,747/59,804 aiv_cc pairs, run-clustered 0.99905 [0.99858, 0.99943] (aiv_accounting/O9); idle gaps of 300 s or more break it in only 8/32 aiv_cc pairs vs 49/59,772 below 300 s, which does not support the stopwatch reading. Content edits that leave usage alone are caught only when large: at realized FPR 0.0101 [0.0092, 0.0112], an inserted change needs 8,913 / 10,000 chars for power 0.5 / 0.9 in swechat CC, and deleting a [100,1000)-char result has power 0.003 (n 61,269) (TC2, TC16 skeptic).
ranking.test_measurement: On swechat sessions with tallies (5,701): delete one assistant message (all records of one message.id), insert a copied message.id, append after the snapshot point, insert a tool_use block into an existing message.id, edit result content; report detection per tamper against the honest 33/5,701, overall and per CLI version. Characterize the swechat CC and cc_local cache-chain breaks (holds 0.975 and 0.982 of clean pairs; only aiv_cc breaks are characterized) before any session-level use of the identities. aiv_cc result rows (211 runs, one agent): delete or insert a response with null stop_reason.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5,701 unexplained (higher in CLI 0.5.x, 15/1,048; 6 of 33 in one repo); the dataset join artifact must be corrected first (it resolves 31 of 64 raw mismatches; T3); 6 Claude 'none' residuals are unexplained (T4 skeptic). Cache-chain breaks in aiv_cc from compaction (0/933 hold), images (4,367/4,570 hold) and idle gaps (8/32), plus 30 unlogged non-compaction resets with no marker (aiv_accounting/O12), which is exactly what an unchanged-prefix certificate would flag. swechat CC chain breaks are uncharacterized (coverage#2 skeptic). Hidden-content tools in conservation (ToolSearch residual median +897.4 with 0 logged chars; TC4).
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - prior art not checked; do not claim new; mostly listed prior art per the grounding skeptics. A commit-time tally acting as a seal overlaps hash-chain sealing (Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric); the Entire CLI is capture-side tooling someone installed (Hearsay/ACE/Tracekit category); per-call conservation is our own Phase A plan; the robustness#2 skeptic shows cache-chain amplification adds nothing against a tolerance-0 tally, and replica independence is unmeasured. The prompt-cache leg may have external prior art (Gu et al. 2025, 'Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs'; relevance unverified).
ranking.why_this_rank: (a) Honest rate measured at tolerance 0 (33/5,701) and 1-API-message resolution by arithmetic, but no tamper rate is measured, and its content power is the existing conservation result (8,913 chars at power 0.5). (b) The tally recounts fields the log already holds; its anchor sits in a local git branch that is rewritable until pushed (push time is not in the data); live fabrication evades it completely because the provider really counted the fake output; every identity is arithmetic a forger can propagate. (c) Identities exist in all five families, but the tally exists only in swechat Entire sessions and the share of turns covered by an exact identity is unmeasured. (d) Cheap: the T1 matcher exists. Last because it constrains which turns exist rather than what results said, and the skeptics call it mostly listed prior art.

build_first: Rank 1, the provider-minted clock bracket. It is the only merged mechanism with both a measured honest rate (10/3,674 swechat streams, 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466]; 1/847 cc_local; analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json ids/O5) and a measured tamper displacement (5 s and 30 s back-dating flag 1,441 and 3,581 of 3,673 streams). The next step reuses existing code, and it has a clean kill rule. First experiment: commit the skeptic's placebo code (scratchpad rd/o5*.py; uncommitted today, so its numbers cannot be cited in FINDINGS until re-run from a committed script) and extend it to single-response tampering: delay one result, insert one fabricated round, splice one response with a foreign request id. Pre-register the kill rule: if single-response insertion or splicing is flagged at a rate whose CI overlaps the honest 10/3,674, stop that tamper type and report the bracket as back-dating-only. This lens already read B and the split-A holdout, so the test set should be cc_local sessions recorded after the Phase C commit. Caveat for whoever builds it: this addresses post-hoc log editing only. If the threat that matters is a lying tool backend, rank 3's printed-duration leg is the only proposal aimed at it, and its first step (the share of results that print a duration at all) is unmeasured and should run before any investment. For GUI-agent logs, rank 2's first step (one-GUI-action insert/delete on aiv_cu Gemini) is equally cheap.
relation_to_phase_b: Interpretation; numbers from analysis/out/probe_{1..4}.json and analysis/notes/probe_{1..4}.md. The four tested mechanisms are behavioural signatures of who produced a result. The five proposals are mostly log-integrity witnesses aimed at post-hoc edits. They answer different threats and do not substitute for each other. Probe 1 (latency physics) is the only tested per-result mechanism to reach ALIVE: swechat/opencode fp 7/4,419 = 0.0016 [0, 0.0033], AUC 0.999 [0.998, 1.000]; cc_local fp 1/1,019 = 0.0010 [0, 0.0033], AUC 0.919 [0.881, 0.971]. It is WEAK in swechat CC (fp 72/20,937 = 0.0034 [0.0025, 0.0044], AUC 0.987 [0.980, 0.993], floor UNSTABLE 21/156), aiv_cc (241/3,217 = 0.075 [0.040, 0.119]) and codex (270/4,329 = 0.062 [0.026, 0.118]), and NOT_TESTABLE in aiv_cu, whowhen and cursor. Its honest per-pair rates are of the same order as rank 1's per-stream 0.00272, but on a different unit. It is one-sided (it catches inline generation of read-type results only) and has no fabricated positive control. Rank 1 does not close Probe 1's natural evasion. Compressing a call->result gap inside one round crosses no request-id time, and the bracket's measured one-sidedness (later output shifts flag only the baseline 10) implies it would not see that; this is reasoning, not measured. coverage#1's stretch-guard claim concerns the opposite direction and is unmeasured. Probe 2 (knowledge precedence): no ALIVE cell. Best S_deep is 0.144 [0.125, 0.163] (671/4,655, swechat CC main) and 0.077 [0.062, 0.091] (subagent). DEAD in opencode main (0.309), codex main (0.311) and cc_local main (0.592); aiv_cu INCONCLUSIVE (0.807). Only the Edit old_string instrument channel is quiet: 0.027 [0.022, 0.031], 1,242/46,836. Probe 3 (pushback): the zero-error tail is ALIVE only in swechat CC, Z = 9/413 = 0.022 W[0.012, 0.041]. It is session-level and evaded by faking one error. DEAD in cc_local (15/36 = 0.417) and aiv_cu (678/988 = 0.686); reaction is at best WEAK everywhere (swechat CC effect 0.106 [0.091, 0.121]). Probe 4 (entropy): hex is WEAK where testable (swechat CC 0.110 [0.041, 0.232]; aiv_cu 0.093 [0.043, 0.216]) and INSUFFICIENT_N in 7 of 9 units. Round numbers are ALIVE in swechat CC (0.423 [0.334, 0.520] vs machine 0.116 [0.110, 0.122]) and cc_local (0.648 [0.435, 0.786] vs 0.121 [0.110, 0.130]) but driven mostly by parameter choices, with no per-result power. Comparison: no proposal has a measured detection rate against a fabricated tool result, and only rank 1 has any measured tamper rate (for timing displacement); every Phase B mechanism also lacks a fabricated positive control. Several proposals have lower, tighter honest rates than Phase B (rank 2: 0/4,134 shell windows with an image increment; rank 4: all 402/88,229 mismatches explained), but honest rates are not detection rates. Phase C measured on split B, which its lenses read before Phase B ran, so neither set is a blind held-out test. Not ranked: Probe 2's quiet channel and commit_witness/O3 and O6 (Edit '+'-line full match 0.829 [0.812, 0.844] vs cross-repo decoy 0.0014 [0.0009, 0.0020]; Write committed-content full 0.843 [0.825, 0.861] vs decoy 0.0011 [0.0003, 0.0022], honest 'none' 0.0016 [0.0005, 0.0029]; analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json) are the strongest external-witness separations in the data. They were not among the 15 proposals, and they overlap the core git shadow-state plan, so I did not rank them. aiv_cc is one agent throughout, and cc_local is aggregates only.
